title: Analysis of Coburn's toe implant: skewed isotopes and nanotech

tellings.quote: Then um he got funding from Haime Masan to uh to remove it a few months later and um he didn't have anybody to analyze it. So um where I was working at the time I had I had [clears throat] access to a lot of analyt analytical equipment.

plain: A small object taken out of the toe of a person named Coburn, believed by some to be an implant placed in the body by non-human beings, was found on analysis to have unusual isotope ratios and features that looked like nanotechnology, which would point to something not made by ordinary means. The researcher Steve Colbern tells Michels he did the analysis himself: Roger Leir, who removed such objects from people, got funding from Haime Masan to take it out a few months after it was found, had no one to study it, and Colbern had analytical equipment where he worked in California. Colbern credits a paper by Coburn on the toe implant.
